content.value_statement: Senior home renovations can overlook fall prevention, lighting, access, and daily comfort. This skill turns a large Chinese renovation knowledge base into practical, room-specific guidance.
actual_capabilities: Reviews flooring, lighting, bathroom, furniture, storage, and layout choices for older residents.
Provides room-specific recommendations from 206 bundled Chinese renovation references.
Creates practical safety checklists for fall, electrical, and accessibility concerns.
Adapts suggestions to the user's layout, household needs, renovation stage, and budget.
Flags structural, property, and waterproofing checks before demolition or plumbing changes.
limitations: It provides general guidance, not licensed architectural, engineering, medical, or construction advice.
Many references reflect Chinese homes and Xi'an renovation practices, so local rules may differ.
It cannot inspect the property or verify dimensions, materials, workmanship, or resident mobility.
Safety-critical recommendations and current building codes require confirmation from qualified local professionals.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Parent's Renovation
use_cases.description: Build a prioritized safety checklist before meeting designers or contractors.
use_cases.target_user: Adult children planning a parent's home

use_cases.title: Review an Accessible Layout
use_cases.description: Check room plans for trip hazards, reach limits, lighting gaps, and unsuitable furniture.

use_cases.title: Improve an Existing Home
use_cases.description: Identify practical upgrades that support changing mobility without requiring a complete renovation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a senior bedroom safety checklist covering floors, lighting, furniture, storage, switches, and nighttime movement.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare matte tile and wood flooring for an older resident with limited balance. Explain safety, maintenance, comfort, and cost tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Home Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this room-by-room renovation plan for fall, lighting, bathroom, storage, and accessibility risks. Prioritize fixes by urgency and permanence.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Phased Renovation Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this floor plan, mobility profile, budget, and local constraints, create a phased senior-home renovation plan with priorities and verification checkpoints.

output_examples.input: My mother wakes twice nightly and the bathroom is across a dark hallway.
output_examples.output: Prioritize continuous low-level lighting, accessible mechanical switches, a clear walking path, non-slip flooring, and stable hand support near the bathroom.

output_examples.input: Should I install glossy tile in my father's bathroom?
output_examples.output: Avoid glossy tile because wet surfaces increase slip risk. Compare rated non-slip matte options and verify drainage, thresholds, and grout maintenance locally.

output_examples.input: We have a limited budget for an older couple's apartment.
output: First fund irreversible safety work, including flooring, electrical placement, waterproofing, and doorway access.
Then improve lighting, bathroom support, furniture edges, and reachable storage.
Add replaceable accessories only after resident needs are confirmed.

best_practices: Share resident mobility, vision, routines, room dimensions, budget, and renovation stage.
Ask for priorities separated into urgent safety work, permanent construction, and later accessories.
Confirm structural, electrical, gas, waterproofing, and code-sensitive changes with qualified local professionals.
anti_patterns: Do not request a final design without providing dimensions, household needs, and local constraints.
Do not treat general guidance as approval for demolition, plumbing, electrical, or gas work.
Do not add technology or accessibility fixtures before confirming the resident can use them comfortably.

faq.question: Does this skill design complete construction drawings?
faq.answer: No. It provides planning guidance and checklists, but a qualified local professional must produce and approve construction documents.

faq.question: Can it review an existing renovation plan?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide room details, dimensions, resident needs, and proposed materials for a focused risk review.

faq.question: Does it cover bathrooms and nighttime safety?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers slip prevention, thresholds, lighting, switches, bathing layouts, support, and clear movement routes.

faq.question: Are recommendations valid outside China?
faq.answer: The principles may help, but materials, construction methods, and regulations require local verification.

faq.question: Can it recommend specific brands or contractors?
faq.answer: No. The guidance focuses on requirements, layouts, risks, and product characteristics rather than specific vendors.

faq.question: What information produces the best answer?
faq.answer: Provide the floor plan, room dimensions, resident mobility, vision, routines, budget, location, and renovation stage.
